summary: Bermond's conjecture that every lobster is graceful remains open. Significant partial results are established: lobsters with an almost perfect matching (a matching covering all but one vertex) are graceful (Krop, 2014); certain families defined by adjacency-matrix constructions are graceful (Ghosh, 2013); and earlier work covers lobsters with a perfect matching and all trees of diameter at most 5. An asymptotic result (Letzter–Pokrovskiy–Williams, 2025) shows every sufficiently large tree has an almost graceful labelling (gracesize ≥ (1−ε)(n−1)), which applies to lobsters but does not resolve the exact conjecture. Gallian's dynamic survey (version November 2026) continues to list the conjecture as open.

notes: Gallian's dynamic survey DS6 (version dated November 2026, confirmed from the journal landing page) is the authoritative ongoing record; the conjecture is still listed as open there. The Letzter–Pokrovskiy–Williams 2025 asymptotic result applies to all trees including lobsters, but only in the almost-graceful sense (not every edge-label achieved, just (1−ε) fraction). No paper settling the full conjecture was found in an extended search through November 2026. The related corpus record is the general Graceful Tree Conjecture (OPG: graceful_tree_conjecture), of which this is the lobster special case.
